prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary (within 500 words)

Time for common sense: trust people, not government. Set families, entrepreneurs and front‑line professionals free; cherish the institutions and traditions that bind us; restore accountability and national self‑government.

Family, schools, students
- Cut taxes for families: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; restore a Married Couple’s Allowance; remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits; “Family Scholarships” to help parents re‑skill after caring.
- Free Schools: heads and governors run schools; rigorous discipline; Progress Centres for disruptive pupils; money follows the pupil; let good schools expand and new parent/faith/charitable schools open; parents can trigger Ofsted and management change.
- Students/universities: no top‑up fees; loan repayments start at £20k income; create permanent endowments to free universities from political control.

Law, order, drugs
- More police, less paperwork; visible policing (“cops in shops”), parish constables; target vandalism and loutish behaviour.
- Persistent young offenders: many more Secure Training Centre places with release tied to results.
- Drugs: mandatory jail for dealers selling to under‑16s; tougher penalties near schools.
- Honesty in sentencing; prisoners work to compensate victims and support families; lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; strengthen victims’ rights and self‑defence laws.

Economy, tax, regulation, pound
- A tax‑cutting government funded by £8bn annual savings without touching schools, NHS, police or defence. Priorities: abolish tax on savings/dividends; raise pensioner allowances by £2,000; restore Married Couple’s Allowance; cut petrol/diesel duty by at least 6p; scrap IR35; targeted business reliefs.
- Simpler, transparent public accounts (National Accounts Commission); regulatory budgets that fall each year; exempt small firms from some rules.
- Keep the pound and enhance Bank of England independence; spending growth within the economy’s trend rate.

NHS and choice
- Match Labour’s spending plans but end political micromanagement. Patient’s Guarantee: maximum waits set by clinical need; if breached, choose another NHS trust or a private hospital at NHS expense.
- Restore ward sister/matron authority; GP and patient choice of hospital; evidence‑based complementary therapies; more nurse‑led care; rapid‑throughput surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; expand hospice funding. Remove tax penalties on private medical cover when affordable.

Older people, pensions, care
- Respect and independence: abolish most taxes on savings; lift a million pensioners out of income tax; increase the basic pension, with extra help for over‑75s; option to consolidate winter fuel/TV licence into a higher tax‑free pension.
- End compulsory annuitisation at 75; consult on funded pension option for younger workers; protect prudent savers from losing homes to unforeseeable long‑term care costs.

Sovereignty, security, asylum, aid, trade
- In Europe, not run by Europe: keep the pound and veto; renegotiate Nice; reserve powers in UK law; complete the single market; fight EU fraud.
- Strong defence in NATO; no EU army outside NATO; back missile defence; maintain nuclear deterrent; fix overstretch and manning.
- Asylum: secure reception centres while applications are decided; presume refusal from safe countries; enforce removal via a new agency.
- Lead for free trade (EU–NAFTA bridge; global free trade by 2020); move toward 0.7% aid, double delivery via charities, insist on good governance.

Stronger society, welfare reform
- Champion civil society: new Office of Civil Society; cut charity VAT (funded from euro‑prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with Britain Works: pay independent providers for jobs gained and kept; Can Work, Must Work guarantee.
- Fairness for disabled people (higher savings limits); rehab‑focused Incapacity Benefit agency; tough national anti‑fraud squad and NI number clean‑up.
- One nation tolerance across race, religion, gender and sexual orientation.

Town and country, transport, environment, culture
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; honest food labelling; cut rural business rates; protect post offices via benefit card; scrap top‑down housebuilding targets; create “Blue Belts”; urban Regeneration Companies; expand homeownership (Right to Buy, rent‑to‑mortgage).
- Transport: long‑term roads/rail plans; Brit Disc for foreign lorries; fair speed limits (up to 80mph where safe); lower fuel duty.
- Environment: meet climate goals via trading, efficiency, renewables; review nuclear; scrap the Climate Change Levy package.
- Culture/media: endow arts via Channel 4 privatisation and Lottery surpluses; single communications regulator; freer ownership with protections; independent, value‑for‑money oversight of BBC; strengthen grassroots and elite sport.

Democracy and the Union
- Power down to effective “free councils”; local referendums for big Council Tax hikes; abolish regional quangos; English Votes for English Laws; stronger Lords via independent appointments and elected element; tougher parliamentary scrutiny; keep First Past the Post. Support the Belfast Agreement with firm security and full decommissioning.

Time to deliver common sense.
